heading: Should I recompress an existing WebP image?
introduction: Try a new encode for a supported still WebP image, with original dimensions kept by default. If ordinary same-format compression finds no smaller result, the original is returned unchanged with 0% reduction.

sections.heading: Choose quality separately from dimensions
sections.body: Keep WebP output and choose Balanced, High quality, Maximum or a separate Target size. Compare the output at the same scale as the original. Image dimensions are preserved.

sections.heading: Keep transparency when you need it
sections.body: WebP can retain transparent areas. Check edges against both light and dark backgrounds after downloading. JPG output is unavailable when a transparent source would have to be flattened.

sections.heading: Keep a result only when it suits the page
sections.body: Compare actual file size, dimensions and visible detail together. A smaller image with unreadable text may be unsuitable. A requested conversion can increase bytes and is reported separately; it is never described as a saving.

seoDescription: Re-encode WebP images locally for website use. Compare file size, dimensions, detail and transparency before replacing an existing image.
